links.comparator_used: Answering from retrieved evidence regardless of its confidence (no retrieval-confidence gate)
links.outcome: Macro F1 for word-level medical fabrication detection
links.effect: Macro F1 rose from 61% to 74% with the retrieval-confidence gate
links.quote: The failure is actionable: a retrieval-confidence gate that abstains on low-confidence evidence raises macro F1 from 61% to 74%, and we release MedFabric, all code, and every baseline.

links.comparator_used: No-evidence baseline (the LLM's own knowledge alone), with gold versus wrong retrieved passages
links.outcome: Macro F1 for fabrication detection by a strong LLM, by evidence condition
links.effect: Scores 91% with the gold passage, but 35% with a wrong passage, which is below its own no-evidence baseline
links.tradeoff: Incorrect retrieved evidence makes detection worse than having no evidence, a new failure mode
links.quote: Our central finding is that detection is governed by evidence correctness rather than fabrication subtlety, since a strong LLM scores 91% with the gold passage but falls to 35%, below its own no-evidence baseline, under a wrong one, a pattern that holds on two benchmarks at two model scales.
